a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L4 records show the closest nitroimidazole analog metronidazole has high human jejunal effective permeability (3.96 × 10^-4 cm/s in both jejunal segments), comparable to the phenylalanine benchmark of 4.1 × 10^-4 cm/s, supporting efficient intestinal absorption for the nitroimidazole core.

Nitroaromatic and azole drugs are not absorption-limited: nifedipine is ~90% absorbed by radiolabel and is BCS class 1/completely absorbed, and ondansetron is well absorbed across the GI tract, so the nitroimidazole/azole query is unlikely to be permeability-limited.

L5 Caco-2 bidirectional records for nitroimidazole-acetamide analogs show high absorptive permeability (A→B 15.3–38.4 × 10^-6 cm/s) with efflux ratios of 0.70–0.97, indicating no gut-wall efflux barrier for this chemotype.
L5 records for nitroimidazole analogs show no metabolism in Caco-2 cells and high recovery, indicating negligible intestinal metabolism; no affirmative evidence supports F below 20%.

L4/L5 permeability and efflux records are for metronidazole and other nitroimidazole analogs, not the query molecule itself.
No query-specific solubility, formulation, prandial state, dose, or species data are supplied.
No query-specific hepatic first-pass or systemic clearance data are supplied.
No human intestinal metabolism data for the exact query are supplied.

No affirmative transferable evidence supports F < 20%, so the high prediction is maintained and strengthened with moderate confidence.
